lines.li: [us] I hear {TOWN} is new.
[them,their:tribal] It is, we followed {FOUNDER} out to a new hearth this year.
[them,their:medieval] It is, {FOUNDER} led us out and holds the charter.
[them,their:spacer] It is, {FOUNDER} filed the charter and we came down with the first habitats.
[them] It is, {FOUNDER} led the first of us out this year.
[us] How is it going?
[them,town:struggling|town:poor] Slowly, but nobody has gone back yet.
[them,!town:struggling,!town:poor] Better than anyone at home said it would.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {TOWN} is a new town, founded this year by settlers under {FOUNDER}.

lines.li: [us] You led the settlers out to {TOWN}, didn't you?
[them,their:tribal] I did, I carried the embers from {MOTHERTOWN} myself.
[them] I did, I walked the first carts out from {MOTHERTOWN} myself.
[us] That's a lot to carry.
[them,town:struggling] Some nights it feels like I carry all of it alone.
[them,!town:struggling] Every family who came is carrying it with me.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {FOUNDER} led the settlers of {TOWN} out from {MOTHERTOWN}.

lines.li: [us] You founded {TOWN}, didn't you?
[them] I did, and some days I wonder what I was thinking.
[us] And other days?
[them] Other days I look at what we built and I know exactly.
[us] Where did your people come from, before {TOWN}?
[them] Out of {MOTHERTOWN}, most of us, with whatever we could carry.
[us] Do you miss it?
[them,their:tribal] The old fires, yes, but a hearth is a hearth.
[them] Some nights, but you can't go back once you've built something.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: The settlers of {TOWN} came out from {MOTHERTOWN}.

lines.li: [us] What made your people settle at {TOWN}?
[them] We came {WHYFOUNDED}.
[us] And will you stay?
[them,town:struggling] If the next season is kinder than the last.
[them,!town:struggling] That's the idea, we didn't put up walls to leave them.
[us] Why build {TOWN} where you did?
[them] For the river, water for the fields and a road that never needs mending.
[us] Until it floods.
[them] We built on the high bank, we're not fools.
[us] Why build {TOWN} where you did?
[them] The road, everything that moves along it stops with us now.
[us] Traders and trouble both.
[them] We have a gate for the one and a welcome for the other.
[us] What brought your people to the coast?
[them] The sea at our door, salt and fish and a way out if we ever need one.
[us] And the storms?
[them] We build low and we build stubborn.
[us] It's hard country around {TOWN}.
[them] That's why we chose it, the hills keep off the wind and the raiders.
[us] All of them?
[them] Enough of them, nobody climbs a hill to be disappointed twice.
[us] Someone told me {TOWN} stands on old walls.
[them] It does, we found them half buried and built on what was sound.
[us] Any idea who built them?
[them,their:tribal] The elders say people like us, and they chose well.
[them] No, but they chose the place well, whoever they were.
[us] Were you at {TOWN} from the start?
[them] Most of us came after the old town was given up, so yes, from the very start.
[us] That must have been hard.
[them] Losing a home is hard, building one is just work.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: Families who lost their homes when a town was given up helped found {TOWN}.

lines.li: [us] Why leave {MOTHERTOWN}, if it was doing so well?
[them] Because it was doing so well, every room was taken and every field spoken for.
[us] So the young ones moved out.
[them] The young and the restless, and a few of us who should know better.
[us] What made you settle at {TOWN}?
[them] The land, it's better than it looks, and nobody had built on it.
[us] That's usually a reason it's empty.
[them] Or a reason nobody looked closely.
[us] What is {FOUNDER} like?
[them,their:tribal] {FOUNDER} listens to the land, and the elders trust that.
[them] Stubborn, which is the only kind of person who starts a town.
[us] And you followed.
[them] Somebody had to carry the other end of everything.
[them] {TOWN} is new, so every friend we make now counts twice.
[us] Then count us.
[them] I will, and I'll tell {FOUNDER} so.
[them] It's our first winter at {TOWN}, and every family is counting the woodpile.
[us] Will you have enough?
[them,town:struggling|town:poor] If it's short, we'll be short of a few things by spring.
[them,!town:struggling,!town:poor] Enough, if the cold doesn't drag on.
[them] It's our first spring at {TOWN}, and the fields we broke are coming up green.
[us] That must feel good.
[them] Like proof, after a year of being told we were mad.
[them] The first harvest at {TOWN} is coming in, and everyone's in the fields.
[us] Good soil?
[them,town:why:land] Better than it looks, as I keep telling people.
[them,!town:why:land] Good enough, we'll know for certain by winter.
[them] The elders lit the new hearth at {TOWN} with embers carried from the old one.
[us] All that way?
[them] In a clay pot, fed every night, so the fire never forgets where it came from.
[them] They read the charter for {TOWN} at the market cross, and now it's a proper town.
[us] What changed?
[them] Nothing at all, except now the tithe collector knows where to find us.
[them] We staked out every street at {TOWN} before the first roof went up.
[us] Planning ahead.
[them] Somebody has to, the last town grew like a weed.
[them] Our charter for {TOWN} is filed, and the habitat seals passed on the first try.
[us] Is that unusual?
[them] Ask anyone who's lived through a second try.
[them] {TOWN} has its charter from the throne now, and a household to fill it.
[us] Is that an honor?
[them] It is a duty, which at court is the same thing.
[them] A new town is a hungry thing, and {TOWN} is hungrier than most.
[us] Lean years are worst at the start.
[them] So they say, and so we hope.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {TOWN}, a new town, is having a hard first year.

lines.li: [them] For a town this young, {TOWN} is holding steady, which surprises everyone.
[us] Including you?
[them] Me most of all.
[us] How are things at {TOWN}?
[them,situation:theirs] Between {SITUATION} and everything else, we're {FORTUNE}.
[them,!situation:theirs] We're {FORTUNE}, if I'm honest.
[us] I'm sorry to hear it.
[them,deed:good] Your people helped mine once, so I'll say it plainly: we could use it again.
[them,!deed:good] We'll get through it, we always have.
[them] We're {FORTUNE} at {TOWN}, but nobody has been turned away from a fire yet.
[us] That says something about your people.
[them] It says we remember being turned away ourselves.
[them] Trade has been bad since {TOWN} fell on hard times, so I hope you're buying.
[us] We'll have a look.
[them] That's all I ask.
[us] How are things at {TOWN}?
[them,their:tribal] Lean, the hunting is thin and the stores are thinner.
[them] Thin, if I'm honest, we're getting by and no more.
[us] I hope it turns.
[them] It will, these things come round.
[them] Things are {FORTUNE} at {TOWN}, so every sale counts this trip.
[us] Then let's see what you have.
[us] How is {TOWN} faring?
[them] Steady, nothing to boast of and nothing to fear.
[us] How is {TOWN} faring these days?
[them,their:medieval] Prospering, the market's full and the tithe was paid early.
[them,their:tribal] Well, the hunts are good and every child is fat.
[them] Thriving, there's work for anyone who wants it.
[us] Glad to hear it.
[them,situation:theirs,situation:good] {SITUATION} has done us a lot of good.
[them] Long may it last.
[them,their:spacer] {TOWN} is booming, every pad is booked and every hand is working.
[them,their:tribal] {TOWN} has never eaten so well, and the elders say it is a sign.
[them] {TOWN} has never done better, there's more work than hands.
[us] What's the secret?
[them,town:why:road] The road, everything comes through us now.
[them,town:why:river] The river, mostly, and people willing to work it.
[them] Good years and people who work, mostly.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {TOWN} is {FORTUNE}, and has never done better.

lines.li: [them] Business is good at {TOWN}, so I can afford to be generous today.
[us] Generous how?
[them] Generous in conversation, mostly, let's not get carried away.
[them] Times are good, good enough that some of our people went off to found {NEWTOWN}.
[us] Will they do as well?
[them] If they work half as hard as they argue, they'll do better.
[them] Have you heard that {NEWTOWNPEOPLE} have founded a new town at {NEWTOWN}?
[us] We heard something of it.
[them,their:tribal] New fires near the old paths, and the elders don't like it.
[them] More neighbors means more trade or more trouble, and we'll see which.
[them] {NEWTOWN} will want everything a new town wants, and a trader could do well there.
[us] Will you go?
[them] If the road is safe, I'll be there before the dust settles.
[them] The Empire has taken note of {NEWTOWN}, as it takes note of everything.
[us] And what does it think?
[them] That it would look better under a proper banner.
[them] Some of our families went out to found {NEWTOWN} this year.
[us] Do you know any of them?
[them] A few by name, and I wish them a gentle first winter.
[us] There's a new town at {NEWTOWN}, did you know?
[them,region:newtown:theirs] Of course, those are our own people out there.
[them,!region:newtown:theirs] Everyone on the road knows by now.
[us] What do you make of it?
[them,region:newtown:theirs] They'll do well, they're stubborn like the rest of us.
[them,!region:newtown:theirs] New neighbors are new mouths, but also new hands.
